facts.title: Djivan Gasparyan
facts.text: Born near Hrazdan, he began teaching himself to play the duduk at age six while living in an orphanage.
He joined the Armenian National Ensemble and played with the Philharmonic without knowing how to read music.

facts.title: Four Gold Medals
facts.text: Under UNESCO sponsorship, he won four gold medals at world competitions in 1959, 1962, 1973, and 1980.

facts.title: Brian Eno
facts.text: The British musician invited him to London, bringing the sound of his instrument to the global stage.

facts.title: Gladiator
facts.text: Hans Zimmer chose his duduk to perform the track To Zucchabar for the film's soundtrack.

facts.title: Eurovision
facts.text: Alongside Eva Rivas, he became the oldest participant in the history of the international contest.

facts.title: 92 Years Old
facts.text: Passing away at age 92, the legendary master was buried at the Komitas Pantheon in Yerevan.

ytTitle: Djivan Gasparyan, the Armenian Duduk Master Who Conquered Hollywood
ytLead: The undisputed master of the duduk, Djivan Gasparyan brought Armenian melodies to the world's most prestigious stages. From his early days in an orphanage to the score of Gladiator, he elevated the apricot wood instrument into a global icon.
